kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: Generic; no manufacturer name is printed on the membrane. This part is sold under many brand labels with the same 4x4 layout.
identity.manufacturer_part_number: None confirmed; a generic 4x4 matrix membrane keypad, the same functional part sold as Adafruit product 3844 and Handson Technology's 4x4 Matrix Membrane Keypad
identity.package: flat flexible plastic membrane with adhesive backing, ending in a ribbon cable with an 8-pin, 0.1 inch pitch connector

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A flat, bendable button pad with 16 keys (0 to 9, A to D, star, and pound) that lets someone type numbers or letters into the Arduino.
function.what_it_is_used_for: User input, for example a door lock code pad, a simple calculator, or menu navigation.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The 16 keys are wired in a grid of 4 rows and 4 columns, so only 8 wires are needed instead of 16. Under each key is a simple switch that, when pressed, connects one row wire to one column wire. The Arduino repeatedly checks each row and column combination (a process called scanning) to work out which single key was pressed.

pinout.name: Row 1 (R1)
pinout.notes: Row pins are on the left side when facing the keypad with the keys up (Handson Technology datasheet)

pinout.name: Column 1 (C1)
pinout.notes: Column pins are on the right side (Handson Technology datasheet)

pins.pin_1_identification: With the keypad facing you, keys up, and the ribbon cable coming off the bottom edge, the first 4 pins on the connector are the rows and the last 4 are the columns (Handson Technology datasheet). ELEGOO's own tutorial wires the first pin to Arduino D9 through the eighth pin to D2, in that same order.

electrical.operating_voltage: No chip onboard, so it works at whatever logic level the microcontroller uses; the switch contacts themselves are rated a maximum of 24VDC / 30mA (Handson Technology datasheet)
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: 24V DC across any single switch contact (Handson Technology datasheet)
electrical.typical_current: Negligible; a plain mechanical switch closure, current is set by the microcontroller's own pull resistor, not by the keypad
electrical.logic_level: None; passive switches only, logic level is whatever the connected microcontroller pins use

key_specs.layout: 4 rows by 4 columns: keys 0-9, A-D, star (*), and pound (#)
key_specs.dimensions: about 69mm x 65.5mm (Adafruit product 3844); Handson Technology's own version lists a very similar 6.9cm x 7.6cm

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Thin, flat, bendable black rectangular pad about 7cm by 7cm, printed with a 4x4 grid of key labels, with a narrow ribbon tail coming off one edge ending in an 8-pin connector
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Black membrane surface with light-colored printed digits 0 to 9, letters A to D, and the star and pound symbols in a 4x4 grid; the ribbon tail is often a different colored film (commonly tan or grey)
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: The key labels themselves: 0-9, A, B, C, D, star, pound. Usually no other printed text on the membrane.
easily_confused_with: a silicone push-button keypad in the same 4x4 layout, which has raised rubber buttons instead of a flat membrane

wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: Keypad library (by Mark Stanley and Alexander Brevig), per ELEGOO's Lesson 11

handling_notes: Do not fold or crease the membrane sharply; it is a flexible film and can crack
The adhesive backing is meant for one-time mounting, so avoid pressing it down until you have chosen a final position
common_mistakes: Wiring the row and column pins in the wrong order without checking the datasheet
Assuming the keymap in the code matches the printed key layout without verifying it

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: The Keypad library is not installed, or the row/column wiring order does not match the code
symptoms_and_causes.check: Confirm the Keypad library is installed (ELEGOO Lesson 1) and that the row/column pin arrays in the sketch match the physical wiring

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: The wrong character shows for a key that is pressed
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Rows and columns swapped, or the keymap array in the code does not match the physical key layout
symptoms_and_causes.check: Compare the keymap array in the sketch against the printed layout on the keypad

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the keypad unplugged from the Arduino, set a multimeter to continuity or resistance mode, touch one probe to a row pin and the other to a column pin, and hold down the key at their intersection. You should read a low resistance only while that specific key is held, and an open circuit otherwise.

typical_suppliers: Amazon (often sold in packs of 2 to 10)

confidence.notes: ELEGOO's own tutorial and the independent Handson Technology datasheet agree on pin order, key count, and layout, so confidence is high despite this being an unbranded generic part. This module is confirmed present in the current EL-KIT-001 kit.
